rules_sent_back.instruction: Give every process and every expanded subProcess its own explicit start event and end event. A trigger that occurs after the main flow (for example later feedback or a return) is joined to the main flow by a gateway, or modeled as an event subprocess or a separate process.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that a trigger occurring after the main flow has ended (for example a later response from the party being served, or a reversal of the delivered goods) may start additional handling

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that an activity is carried out alongside a monitoring or follow-up activity that runs at the same time (joined by 'and' or 'while'), and a later step is reached only after both are finished: Model a parallel gateway that splits into the concurrent activities, and a parallel gateway that joins them before the next step. Do not model the concurrent activities as one sequential chain, and do not add conditions to the branches.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that two activities, each carried out by a different team or system, are joined by 'and' in one sentence with no order given between them, and a later step is described as following only after both are complete

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description offers an either-or choice between two named ways of carrying out one step (for example 'X or Y'), and both ways continue to the same following step: Model each named way as its own task or path. Place an exclusive gateway before the alternatives to split the flow, with one outgoing branch per alternative. Join the alternative branches with an exclusive gateway before the common next step. Do not drop an alternative, and do not collapse the alternatives into one generic activity.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that the case begins when an actor performs an action through one of several alternative channels joined by 'or', where each channel is a distinct way of performing that same action

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says the process waits until an external milestone is reached (for example, an item arriving at a recipient's location) and later steps depend on that milestone having occurred: Model the wait as an intermediate catch event, not a task, and name that catch event with the milestone as the description states it, so the stage stays identifiable in the model. Do not replace the wait with a task, and do not leave the milestone unnamed or rename it to a generic label.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says the process waits until an external milestone is reached (for example, an item arriving at a recipient's location) and later steps depend on that milestone having occurred

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description lists several activities of a stage with no order stated between them, and the stage or the process ends only after all of those activities are finished: Model a parallel gateway directly after the task that starts the stage or precedes the list. Fork it into one task per listed activity, each as its own task with the action the description gives for it. Connect every one of those tasks into a second parallel gateway that joins them. Place the join before the next step or the end event, and connect it onward from there. Do not chain the unordered activities in sequence, and do not use an exclusive gateway for either the fork or the join.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description names two activities joined by 'and' in one clause, performed by different teams or systems with no order stated between them, and a later step is reached only after both are finished

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says an activity is carried out repeatedly until a stated condition is reached, so the activity repeats until the condition holds, and the process moves on only after that point: Model the repeated activity as a single task, followed by an exclusive gateway that checks whether the stated condition has been reached. Give one outgoing sequence flow that loops back to the repeated task while the condition is not met, and one outgoing sequence flow that leads to the next step once it is met. Do not model the repetition as an unconditional sequence of separate tasks, and do not leave the exit condition implicit.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says an activity is carried out repeatedly until a stated condition is reached, so the activity repeats until the condition holds, and the process moves on only after that point
